overview: Diabetes is a chronic condition that occurs when the body cannot properly regulate blood sugar (glucose) levels. There are two main types: Type 1 (autoimmune, insulin-dependent) and Type 2 (lifestyle-related, insulin resistance).

types.name: Type 1 Diabetes
types.description: An autoimmune condition where the pancreas produces little or no insulin. Requires daily insulin injections.

types.name: Type 2 Diabetes
types.description: The most common form. The body doesn't use insulin well. Managed with lifestyle changes, oral medications, or insulin.

types.name: Gestational Diabetes
types.description: Occurs during pregnancy and usually resolves after birth, but increases risk of Type 2 later.

symptoms: Darkened skin in body creases (acanthosis nigricans)
diagnosis: Fasting Blood Sugar Test (FBS) — normal: <100 mg/dL

lifestyle: Healthy diet rich in fiber, low in refined carbs

emergency_signs: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA): fruity breath, vomiting, confusion

faqs.question: Can diabetes be cured?
faqs.answer: Type 1 has no cure. Type 2 can go into remission with significant lifestyle changes, but requires ongoing management.

faqs.question: Is diabetes hereditary?
faqs.answer: Yes, genetic factors play a role, but lifestyle choices significantly influence whether someone develops Type 2 diabetes.

faqs.question: What foods should diabetics avoid?
faqs.answer: Sugary drinks, white bread, processed snacks, fried foods, and high-sugar fruits in large quantities should be limited.
